programme: BCL6 and HDAC1 form a transcriptional corepressor axis: BCL6 is the canonical repressor that recruits HDAC-containing corepressor complexes (the MTA3–NuRD/HDAC1-2 and SMRT/NCoR arms of BCL6 biology) to silence differentiation-checkpoint genes in lymphocytes, controlling the balance between follicular helper (Tfh), regulatory, and Th17-like effector states.
role_in_a: In IBS, HDAC1 is reported to act at the intestinal epithelial/mucosal level, with two directly-on-topic papers describing HDAC1-linked epigenetic regulation of gut epithelial genes under chemical and metabolic stress (cinnamaldehyde network-pharmacology model; methylglyoxal effects on epigenetic enzymes). BCL6's own placement in IBS is weak here — the only retrieved 'BCL6' paper is actually about Zbtb20, a related BTB-ZF factor, in gut-derived Treg cells, not BCL6 itself.
role_in_b: In MS, BCL6 is directly implicated: it promotes CCR2-driven CNS infiltration of encephalitogenic Th17 cells, and follicular regulatory/helper T cell biology built on BCL6 supports B-cell-driven EAE pathology — three papers converge on a BCL6-dependent Tfh/Th17/B-cell axis in CNS autoimmunity. HDAC1's MS evidence is thinner: the one retrieved paper places HDAC1-driven microglial activation in a post-stroke context, not MS proper, so it is neuroinflammation-adjacent rather than MS-specific.
shared_axis: If the same BCL6-HDAC1 corepressor module that shapes germinal-center/Tfh/Th17 lymphocyte fate in CNS-infiltrating cells in MS also operates in mucosal lymphocytes and epithelium in the gut, that would explain why cohorts from both diseases converge on this pair: not a shared disease mechanism per se, but a shared lymphocyte-differentiation toolkit deployed in two different inflamed tissues.
reasoning: The module is nameable and immunologically real (BCL6 is a well-characterized HDAC-recruiting repressor), and each factor is solidly placed in one disease — BCL6 in MS/EAE Th17-CNS biology, HDAC1 in IBS epithelial regulation — but the cross-placements are weak (BCL6's IBS paper is about a different gene; HDAC1's MS paper is about stroke, not MS), so the claim that one shared module operates in both diseases rests on reasoning about the complex's known biology, not on retrieved evidence that ties both diseases to the same factor.
support: PMID 42048739 — BCL6 drives CCR2-dependent Th17 CNS infiltration in EAE, direct MS-model mechanism; PMID 40864683 — follicular regulatory T cells promote EAE via B-cell support, BCL6-dependent Tfh/Tfr biology in an MS model; PMID 41633306 — reviews Tfh/peripheral/resident helper cell biology in B-cell-driven disease, MS-relevant context for BCL6; PMID 42500261 — HDAC1 implicated via network pharmacology in IBS; PMID 41355505 — HDAC1-linked epigenetic regulatory enzyme changes in intestinal cells, IBS-relevant; PMID 41388741 — HDAC1 dysregulation drives microglial activation, but in post-stroke rather than MS tissue, so only loosely applicable; PMID 35522722 — retrieved under BCL6 but its subject is Zbtb20, a paralogous factor, in gut Treg cells, so it does not directly support BCL6 in IBS.
how_to_falsify: In parallel ChIP-seq (or CUT&RUN) for BCL6 and HDAC1 done on CNS-infiltrating Th17/Tfh cells from an EAE model and on colonic mucosal lymphocytes/epithelium from an IBS model, test whether the two factors co-occupy a shared target-gene set (e.g., CCR2/IL17 pathway genes) in both tissues. If BCL6 and HDAC1 binding do not overlap, or if HDAC1 inhibition fails to phenocopy BCL6 loss-of-repression at the same loci in both tissue contexts, the shared-module account is falsified.
caveats: Tissue pairing is brain vs. colorectal, so any shared axis must run through migratory/mucosal-associated lymphocyte populations rather than tissue-resident glia or enterocytes themselves. 104 patient-group comparisons come from only 3 independent cohort pairs, so the apparent breadth of concordance is not 3 independent confirmations, not 104. FOXP3, the master Treg transcription factor, was removed as tissue-generic — this account deliberately does not lean on general 'Treg dysfunction' as the shared story, only on the more specific BCL6-HDAC1 repressor-complex mechanism, since invoking Treg-centric biology would reach for a factor that was excluded by design. DEAF1 and CIC were considered and dropped: DEAF1's retrieved paper concerns rheumatoid arthritis, not MS, and CIC's retrieved papers are dominated by an unrelated meaning of the acronym (chronic idiopathic constipation / clean intermittent catheterization), so neither survives as evidence rather than as noise.
